title: Terminal
welcome: Nexus shell. Type [1mhelp[22m for commands, [1mman <command>[22m for details, Tab to complete.
pagerStatus: lines {first}–{last} of {total} · Space/b page · ↑/↓ line · q quit

err.binary: {path}: Binary file (use open, or view it in the File Explorer)
err.same: {path}: Source and destination are the same
err.notFound: {name}: command not found. Type “help” for a list.

out.dfFiles: {files} files and {folders} folders in Nexus, {trash} in the trash
out.helpFooter: man COMMAND for details · Tab completes · ↑/↓ history · Ctrl+R search · Ctrl+C stop · Ctrl+L clear

cd.details: Without a folder, goes to your home folder. “cd -” returns to the previous folder; “~” is home.

ls.details:
-l long format (size, date, tags)   -a show hidden files   -h human sizes
-t newest first   -S largest first   -r reverse   -1 one per line

cat.details: -n numbers the lines. Without files, prints the piped input.

less.details: Space/b: page down/up · ↑/↓ or j/k: line · g/G: start/end · q: quit

head.details: Shows 10 lines unless -n says otherwise (also: head -5).

tail.details: Shows 10 lines unless -n says otherwise (also: tail -5).

touch.summary: create empty files or update their date

mkdir.details: -p creates missing parent folders and doesn't complain about existing ones.

rm.details:
Items go to the Trash, so you can restore them in the File Explorer.
-r folders and their contents   -f ignore missing files   -P delete permanently

mv.details: With several sources, DEST must be a folder. A file that would be overwritten goes to the trash first; -n keeps existing files instead.

cp.details: -r copies folders with their contents. A file that would be overwritten goes to the trash first; -n keeps it instead.

find.summary: search for files by name or type
find.details: Patterns use * ? [abc]; quote them so the shell doesn't expand them: find . -name "*.md"

tree.summary: show a folder as a tree
tree.details: -a hidden files   -d folders only   -L how deep to go

du.details: Sizes in KB (-h for readable sizes). -s only the total   -a files too

echo.details: -n no newline at the end   -e understand \n, \t and \e (for colours)

grep.summary: find lines that match a pattern
grep.details:
PATTERN is a regular expression.
-i ignore case   -n line numbers   -r search folders   -v non-matching lines
-c count   -l file names only   -w whole words   -F plain text, not a pattern

sort.details: -r reverse   -n by number   -u drop duplicates   -f ignore case

uniq.details: -c count   -i ignore case   -d only repeated   -u only unique. Usually after sort.

man.summary: show the manual of a command

uptime.summary: how long Nexus has been running

date.details: -u in UTC   -I ISO date   -R RFC format

export.details: NAME=VALUE on its own line works too. Use them as $NAME.

alias.details: alias ll='ls -la' makes “ll” run “ls -la”. Aliases are saved for all tabs.

history.details:
!N runs entry N again, !! the last one, !-2 the one before, !text the newest starting with text.
-c clears the history.

open.details: Files open with their default app, folders in the File Explorer. Apps by id (nexus.files) or name (files).

apps.details: -a include hidden apps   -l with category and version

kill.details: WINDOW is a window id (nexus.files#1), an app id (closes all its windows) or a number from ps.

theme.details: Without a name, lists the themes (● marks the current one). “theme auto” follows the system.

wallpaper.details: An image file from your files, or a built-in wallpaper id. Without an argument, shows the current one.

calc.details: + - * / % ^, parentheses, pi, e, and functions like sqrt, sin, log, round. Quote expressions with * or ( ): calc '2 * (3 + 4)'

nexusfetch.summary: system information with the Nexus logo

sleep.summary: wait a number of seconds (Ctrl+C stops)

which.summary: tell where a command comes from
